intro_script: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 13, 2026. Today we cover Agile Robots' funding, XPENG's UK expansion, and Viam Launchpad's deployment goals. Stay informed.
outro_script: And that's all the circuits for today's dive into the world of robotics. Agile Robots is really setting the pace! Thanks for tuning in; keep those algorithms humming! See you tomorrow.

items.title: Agile Robots raises $500 million at $8.5 billion valuation
items.summary: Agile Robots raised $500 million in a Series F round, achieving an $8.5 billion valuation. The company plans to use the funds for U.S. expansion, increased production capacity in Germany, and market entry. Agile has deployed over 20,000 robotic solutions across various industries. Production targets differ between large legged/wheeled humanoids and smaller research models planned for 2027. The Agile ONE SN integrates Nvidia's technology for research applications and is expected to be available in early 2027.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, Agile Robots raises five hundred million dollars at an eight point five billion valuation. This report details the recent financing round and the subsequent strategic plans for the company. Agile Robots secured five hundred million dollars in a Series F funding round, establishing an eight point five billion valuation for the firm. The capital is designated for United States expansion, increased production capacity within Germany, and broader market entry initiatives. The company has deployed more than twenty thousand robotic solutions across diverse industrial sectors. Production targets are set for 2027, differentiating between large legged and wheeled humanoids, alongside smaller research models. The Agile ONE SN integrates Nvidia technology for research applications and is projected for availability in early 2027. This development indicates continued investment and expansion within the advanced robotics and artificial intelligence sector.

items.title: XPENG expands UK operations with new vehicles, robotaxis and humanoid robots
items.summary: XPENG is expanding its UK presence by introducing a new vehicle portfolio and plans to integrate its physical AI vision. The company will offer five new right-hand-drive models within 12 months, focusing on intelligent driving technology and dual-energy solutions. XPENG aims to establish a nationwide network of 100 retail and service locations and secure 20 key partnerships by 2027. Beyond vehicles, XPENG is developing a broader physical AI ecosystem, including Robotaxi services and humanoid robots. The company seeks to become the UK's number one premium EV brand by 2028 by focusing on an exceptional customer experience.

items.title: Viam Launchpad aims to accelerate robotics deployments
items.summary: Viam offers a software platform that acts as an abstraction layer for building and deploying hardware systems, enabling robotics startups to move quickly from prototypes to market. This platform helps founders overcome obstacles in building and deploying physical AI by providing the necessary infrastructure. Viam Launchpad provides an intensive program offering founders technical support, resources, and access to hardware labs to facilitate commercial implementation. The platform has already helped startups like Gambit achieve real-world deployments by streamlining the process of connecting hardware with software. Ultimately, Viam aims to accelerate the deployment of physical AI by lowering the barriers for robotics entrepreneurs.

items.title: GXO targets 1,000 Apptronik Apollo robots, Koetsier reports
items.summary: GXO Logistics has a letter of intent with Apptronik to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoids starting in 2027. This four-year plan targets a cost of $15 an hour for the robots. The planned work involves tasks such as picking, packing, and sorting goods within warehouses. The deployment emphasizes the need for dexterity, reliable manipulation, speed, uptime, and autonomy. GXO has previously conducted over 45 humanoid pilots across various vendors.

The proposed deployment encompasses tasks such as picking, packing, and sorting goods inside warehouses, emphasizing requirements for dexterity, reliable manipulation, speed, uptime, and autonomy in the robotic systems. This development signals increased industrial interest in applying advanced humanoid robotics for complex logistical operations.

items.title: The Sequence Robotics - Issue #971: Robots Should Learn on the Job
items.summary: Tutor Intelligence is developing a method for robots to learn through on-the-job experience guided by remote human tutors. This process uses real-world work interventions as training data to improve robot intelligence. A system involving a 100-robot research fleet and a real-to-sim-to-real loop called TRACE provides additional practice. The company's goal is to create an apprenticeship model where the work itself supplies part of the learning curriculum. The core questions involve the efficacy of real-world practice and the reliability of simulated learning results.
items.audio_script: From thesequence.substack.com, The Sequence Robotics - Issue 971 reports on a method for robots to learn through on-the-job experience guided by remote human tutors. This research involves using real-world work interventions as training data to improve robot intelligence. The system incorporates a research fleet of one hundred robots and a process termed TRACE, which facilitates a real-to-sim-to-real loop for additional practice. The development aims to establish an apprenticeship model where the work itself forms part of the learning curriculum. Core investigation centers on the efficacy of real-world practice and the reliability of simulated learning outcomes. This work suggests a pathway toward integrating practical experience directly into robotic training protocols. The findings indicate a method for enhancing machine learning through contextual, real-world application. Future developments will focus on scaling this apprenticeship model across various industrial applications.

items.title: Welcome, Pelican Unify 1.0!
items.summary: Pelican Unify 1.0 is an embodied AI foundation model developed by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X Humanoid). Released on May 14, 2026, it resides in the software layer of robotics, not physical hardware. It has a Humanoid Guide Brain Score of 5 out of 10, indicating it is an emerging software offering. Prospective users should evaluate the model separately from complete robotic systems when considering its use. The model is currently available on backorder, and further details are available on the official website.

items.title: Welcome, LingBot-Touch!
items.summary: LingBot Touch is a software foundation model from Robbyant, focused specifically on touch, positioning it separately from physical robot hands or humanoid platforms. It was trained on nearly 5,000 hours of touch recordings from gloves and robot hands, making tactile data central to its identity. The model is intended to complement other robot software rather than function as an independent controller, scoring a Humanoid Guide Brain Score of 5 out of 10. It is best understood as a specialized component within a larger embodied AI system, distinguished from the surrounding hardware and control software. The project highlights growing research attention to tactile data in embodied AI.

items.title: Helping robots fit into the human workplace
items.summary: Robust AI develops robots designed to complement human capabilities in factory and warehouse settings. Their mobile robot, Carter, is designed to fit alongside humans, featuring force-sensitive handlebars and AI vision for intuitive human control. The company prioritizes systems where humans have agency and input to guide the overall process. Robots are deployed to assist with tasks like picking, stocking, and moving items in logistics and manufacturing. The development philosophy focuses on creating systems that accelerate human tasks rather than simply replacing them.
